rows.Front / theory: Affirmative retroactive rent abatement / reasonable rental value
rows.Authority: Quevedo v. Braga; Smith v. David; Green
rows.Exact trigger / elements: Material habitability breach during paid-rent period; defect affects unit/common area used by tenant; tenant proves duration and reduction in fair rental value.
rows.Potential legal effect / remedy: Affirmative refund of rent overpayment measured by contract rent paid minus reasonable rental value in defective condition; California authority recognizes that an extreme total breach can theoretically reduce reasonable rental value to zero, but this is factual and exceptional.
rows.Clock: Limitations and tenancy-period specific; no automatic full-rent refund.
rows.Likely defense: Defect de minimis, brief, unrelated to claimant/common area, or defective-condition rental value remained close to contract rent.
rows.Plaintiff-side answer / proof needed: Month-by-month defect chronology + rent-paid ledger + comparable/rent-value expert + percentage-loss-of-use evidence; separately prove tort/statutory damages.

rows.Authority: Salazar v. Maradeaga; Gruzen v. Henry
rows.Exact trigger / elements: The occupancy/use itself is illegal under zoning/building law enacted for public benefit and the illegality is uncorrectable, not merely a correctable habitability defect.
rows.Potential legal effect / remedy: Lease can be void/unenforceable; landlord not entitled to back rent under cited line of cases; tenant also may lack possessory right absent separate local protection.
rows.Primary defendant(s) if facts fit: Landlord of any illegally created/occupied unit
rows.Likely defense: All units lawfully permitted/occupied; any defects are correctable maintenance issues rather than illegal use.
rows.Plaintiff-side answer / proof needed: Certificate of occupancy + approved unit count/layout + unit numbering + alteration permits + as-built plan comparison.

rows.Front / theory: JCO economic-displacement relocation after large rent increase
rows.Exact trigger / elements: JCO-covered tenancy + proposed rental increase exceeds the lesser of CPI-All Urban Consumers + 5% or 10% over the ordinance measurement period.
rows.Potential legal effect / remedy: Tenant who elects to relinquish tenancy can be entitled to relocation assistance; current ordinance formula is 3× comparable Los Angeles Metro HUD FMR + $1,411 moving costs, subject to statutory details/offsets.
rows.Clock: Triggered by proposed increase; landlord payment process follows ordinance.
rows.Likely defense: Increase below threshold; tenancy/unit outside JCO; tenant does not elect statutory relinquishment route; amount/offset rules reduce payment.
rows.Plaintiff-side answer / proof needed: Preserve every post-acquisition rent-increase notice; calculate threshold from lawful pre-increase rent and current CPI/FMR; compare notice and payment/escrow compliance.
